title: Optimization: Data Assumptions & Sensitivity Scrub — Finance Prep
content:
Purpose: quick internal scrub of the Optimize cost model assumptions ahead of the finance review next week. Goal is to enumerate data sources, calibration steps taken, open questions for finance sign-off, and sensitivity slices we want modeled in the spreadsheet.

Summary of what we validated so far:
- Billing export reconciliation: matched hosted API token-level billing for Aug–Oct 2025 against model input 'hosted_per_token_cost' and 'tokens_per_request' distributions. Residual variance ~3.2% after mapping free-tier credits. Source: billing-export-2025-08-10_2025-10.csv (finance bucket).
- Dedicated capacity unit economics: cross-check of monthly reserved GPU price (commit contract) vs observed effective cost when utilization < 70%. Used data from committed-capacity-report-2025Q3.xlsx and infra-costs.csv. We observed 18% uplift in per-token cost when utilization drops below target.
- Latency SLO impact on batching: empirical traces from observability (prometheus/trace samples) used to estimate feasible average batch sizes under 95th percentile latency targets. Live runs on p100/rtx8000 staging cluster used as calibration; see trace-set-2025-10-15.json.
- Quantization/throughput lift: microbenchmarks run for int8 dynamic quantization vs fp16. Benchmarks provided speedup and memory reduction numbers but we applied a conservative 75% of measured throughput lift to avoid overfitting to small model artifact timing.

Key assumptions documented (spreadsheet keys in parentheses):
- Average prompt + response token distribution (tokens_per_request): mixture model t-dist; mean=210, median=73 (derived from hosted-call-sample-2025-10-01.csv).
- Batch efficiency curve (batch_efficiency_pct_by_len): empirical piecewise: low seq <=128 -> 1.0x; 129-512 -> 1.6x; >512 -> 2.1x (staging traces).
- Cache hit rate (kv_cache_prefix_pct): baseline 12%, optimistic 28% for heavy-prefix workloads; cache assumed to reduce decode tokens by 85% on hit (KV caching applied only for streaming sessions).
- Reserved capacity discount applied: 10% effective discount after amortized overhead and support (from legal/finance term sheet).
- Spot vs dedicated mix: hosted workload assumes 20% spot equivalent for overflow; dedicated assumes 0% spot.

Sources used and trust notes:
- Billing exports (high trust): direct, but need mapping rules documented for free credits and refunds. Finance owns canonical mapping.
- Prometheus/traces (medium trust): sampling bias present; tail-latency undercount possible. Need SRE to run focused tail runs.
- Benchmarks (low->medium trust): microbenchmarks on small batch sizes — we scaled conservatively. Must add a note: GPU generation differences (A100 vs H100) change kernel behavior; our current profile mixes both.
- Contractual pricing documents (high trust): committed-contract-terms-2025.pdf used for discount, but ops fees/overheads in committed buckets require verification with sales.

Calibration steps taken (what we did to make numbers defensible):
1) Reconciled token counts using a sample of 10k hosted calls; adjusted tokens_per_request distribution to equal weighted average across endpoints.
2) Applied an uplift factor for cross-region egress and support overhead (1.08x) derived from infra-costs.csv line items.
3) For batch efficiency we used a 90th-percentile latency SLO and computed effective throughput multiplier by running synthetic traces at p95 observed latencies.
4) Sensitivity: generated +/- 20% scenarios on key levers: tokens_per_request, batch efficiency, cache hit rate, reserved discount.

Open questions and risks for finance sign-off:
- Residuals in billing reconciliation: 3.2% variance flagged — finance needs to sign off on tolerable threshold. If finance requires <1%, we need to run a full-account-level audit.
- Geographical cost differentials: model currently uses blended region pricing. Finance may require region-by-region P&L which would change unit costs significantly for APAC.
- Treatment of developer/free-tier: current spreadsheet treats free-tier offset as negative cost to revenue; legal flagged potential recognition differences. Coordinate with accounting.
- Quantization adoption curve: we assume conservative adoption (25% of traffic on quantized models by Q3 2026). Product should provide a short adoption roadmap for finance.
- Tail-latency effects: batching improves unit cost but can violate p99 SLOs at spikes. Need SRE to provide rehearsed storm tests to quantify cost of keeping latency SLO during spikes.

Decision points for meeting with Finance (what we will ask them to agree to):
1) Accept blended unit costs with documented regional sensitivity slices OR require region-level costing.
2) Approve current conservative quantization uplift factor (75% of microbenchmarked speedup) or mandate additional H100/A100 parity runs.
3) Accept the 3.2% reconciliation variance as immaterial or require a full audit.
4) Approve modeling of reserved capacity discounts as applied (10% effective) and sign off on amortization window (12 months vs 24 months).

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Asha: prepare a 1-pager with top 5 levers and sensitivity charts for finance slide deck (due 2025-11-14).
- Liam: run dedicated region-level cost extraction and produce APAC/EMEA/NA splits (JIRA-OPT-721-subtask) (due 2025-11-18).
- Maya: schedule SRE tail latency storm runs and export traces (due 2025-11-16).
- Ethan: rerun microbenchmark suite on homogeneous H100 runners and provide raw results + scripts (due 2025-11-15).
- Sofia: check accounting treatment of credits and draft note for legal (due 2025-11-13).

Notes to reviewers (quick, informal):
- This doc is intentionally a working scrub — expect shorthand and loose phrasing. If you care about a number, call it out with a comment and tag finance@redwood.
- We purposely biased conservative on performance uplift to avoid overpromising to finance; if finance wants aggressive scenarios, we can add an "optimistic" tab.
- The spreadsheet tabs referenced: "base_case", "sensitivity_matrix", "region_split_candidate". I will freeze the base_case once we get finance nod.

Appendix (quick pointers to files):
- hosted-call-sample-2025-10-01.csv (raw sample in drive)
- committed-capacity-report-2025Q3.xlsx (contracts folder)
- infra-costs.csv (infra team shared)
- trace-set-2025-10-15.json (observability exports)

Unresolved/parking lot items:
- Need to decide whether to model caching benefits as elastic (user-level) or static per-route — product preference?
- Should we model incremental overhead for multi-tenant isolation (Dedicated customers that require extra isolation)? Needs security/solutions input.

If you want to push back on any assumption, reply inline or add a comment in the sheet. I'll consolidate and produce the finance-ready one-pager.

-- Asha
